    Class "trackStyle"

    trackStyle-class.Rd

    An object of class "trackStyle" represents track style.

    An object of class "track" bundles the genomic data to be plotted together with the style used to draw it. A track is the basic unit accepted by viewTracks; several of them are collected into a trackList for a multi-panel figure.

    # S4 method for class 'track'
seqlevels(x)

# S4 method for class 'track'
seqlevelsStyle(x)

# S4 method for class 'track'
seqlevelsStyle(x) <- value

# S4 method for class 'track'
show(object)

# S4 method for class 'track'
x$name

# S4 method for class 'track'
x$name <- value

# S3 method for class 'track'
.DollarNames(x, pattern = "")

# S3 method for class 'trackStyle'
.DollarNames(x, pattern = "")

setTrackStyleParam(ts, attr, value)

# S4 method for class 'track,character'
setTrackStyleParam(ts, attr, value)

setTrackXscaleParam(ts, attr, value)

# S4 method for class 'track,character'
setTrackXscaleParam(ts, attr, value)

setTrackYaxisParam(ts, attr, value)

# S4 method for class 'track,character'
setTrackYaxisParam(ts, attr, value)

    Arguments

    x

    an object of trackStyle or track

    value

    values to be assigned.

    object

    an object of trackStyle.

    name

    slot name of trackStyle or track

    pattern

    A regular expression. Only matching names are returned.

    ts

    An object of track.

    attr

    the name of slot of trackStyle object to be changed.

    Value

    An object of class track with the modified style, returned invisibly. The variable supplied as ts is updated as a side effect.

    An object of class track with the modified xscale, returned invisibly. The variable supplied as ts is updated as a side effect.

    An object of class track with the modified yaxis, returned invisibly. The variable supplied as ts is updated as a side effect.

    Details

    The validity method enforces the type-specific requirements summarised above; the most common errors are a missing score or feature metadata column, a lollipop range wider than one base, and a dat2 whose length does not match dat for interaction data.

    Note that dat and dat2 are plain GRanges objects, so the seqlevel style of the track must match that of the other tracks and of the plotting range. seqlevelsStyle and its replacement method are defined for track and rename both dat and dat2 at once.

    setTrackStyleParam changes one styling slot of the trackStyle object held in ts@style. It accepts only the slots that are plain values; the two compound slots have their own setters, setTrackXscaleParam for xscale and setTrackYaxisParam for yaxis. Passing any other name, including "xscale" or "yaxis", raises an error.

    Accepted values of attr:

    tracktype

    "character". How the data is drawn. For "data" tracks use "peak" (the default), "line", "histogram" or "annotation", the last marking peak regions rather than plotting their scores. For "interactionData" tracks use "heatmap" or "link".

    color

    "character" vector of colors. Give two values when the track has both dat and dat2, the first for the positive side and the second for the negative side of the baseline.

    height

    "numeric" between 0 and 1, the fraction of the figure given to this track. Note that trackList rewrites this slot for every element it is given, so set it after building the list, not before.

    marginTop, marginBottom

    "numeric", space left above and below the drawing region of the track, as a fraction of its height. Defaults are 0 and 0.05.

    ylim

    "numeric" of length 2 fixing the y-axis range. Useful for making two tracks directly comparable, since the range is otherwise taken from the data in the current view.

    ylabpos

    "character", one of "left", "right", "topleft", "bottomleft", "topright", "bottomright", "abovebaseline", "underbaseline" or "none"; for gene-type tracks also "upstream" or "downstream".

    ylablas

    "numeric" in {0, 1, 2, 3}, the rotation of the y label. See par:las.

    ylabgp

    "list" of graphical parameters for the y label, converted to gpar, e.g. list(cex=.8, col="gray30").

    breaks

    "numeric" breaks for the color key of interaction data.

    NAcolor

    "character", the color used for missing cells of an interaction heatmap. Default "white".

    ysplit

    "numeric", where to split the y region for back-to-back interaction plots. Default 0.5 splits it evenly; it has no effect on other layouts.

    The value is assigned with check = TRUE, so the validity method of trackStyle runs on every call and an out-of-range value (an unknown tracktype, an ylablas outside 0:3, an unrecognized ylabpos) fails immediately rather than at plotting time.

    setTrackXscaleParam changes the x-scale bar of a track, stored as an xscale object at ts@style@xscale. The x-scale bar is a short horizontal ruler drawn inside the track's own panel, independent of the shared genomic x-axis of the whole figure, typically used to show a distance such as "1K" next to a zoomed-in feature.

    attr can be any slot of xscale, or the convenience name "position":

    from, to

    Objects of class pos, the two endpoints of the scale bar. Because these are pos objects rather than bare numbers, setting them directly means constructing the object yourself, e.g. new("pos", x=12345678, y=0.5, unit="native") for a point given in native (genomic) coordinates, or a fraction with unit="npc" for a position relative to the panel. Most callers will find attr="position" (below) more convenient than setting from and to separately, since it keeps them centered and in sync with the label.

    label

    "character", the text drawn on the scale bar, e.g. "500 bp". Set directly this is used verbatim.

    gp

    "list" of graphical parameters for the scale bar and its label, converted to gpar, e.g. list(cex=.5, col="black", lwd=2).

    draw

    "logical", whether the scale bar is drawn at all. Default FALSE; set to TRUE even from/to (or position) have been set, the scale bar will show.

    position

    A shortcut that sets from, to and label together from a single scale length, instead of requiring two pos objects. value must be a "list" with named elements x, y and label:

    • x, y — the native-coordinate of the bar (genomic position and track-relative y, respectively). The bar is drawn symmetrically about this point.

    • label — the width the bar should represent.

    A label that cannot be coerced to numeric (NA after as.numeric) is rejected before any slot is touched.

    As with the other slots of xscale, updated values are assigned with check = TRUE, so the pos validity method (checking the unit string) still applies when from/to are set through "position".

    setTrackYaxisParam changes the y-axis of a track, stored as a yaxisStyle object at ts@style@yaxis. This is the axis drawn alongside the track's own data panel (score, coverage, etc.), separate from the shared genomic x-axis of the whole figure.

    Accepted values of attr, all slots of yaxisStyle:

    at

    "numeric" vector of y-values at which tick marks are drawn, e.g. c(0, 25, 50). If left at its default (numeric(0)), tick positions are chosen automatically from the plotted range.

    label

    "logical", whether the numeric value of each tick in at is printed next to it. Default FALSE, i.e. ticks are drawn without their values; set to TRUE to show them.

    gp

    "list" of graphical parameters for the axis line, ticks and labels, converted to gpar, e.g. list(cex=.6, col="blue", lwd=1.5).

    draw

    "logical", whether the y-axis is drawn at all. Default TRUE.

    main

    "logical", which side of the panel the axis is drawn on: TRUE (the default) draws it on the left of the track, FALSE on the right. Useful for telling apart the axes of two adjacent or back-to-back tracks at a glance.

    Any other value of attr, including "xscale" or a slot name belonging to trackStyle itself (like "color" or "height"), is rejected, use setTrackStyleParam for the plain style slots and setTrackXscaleParam for the x-scale bar. Values are assigned with check = TRUE, so an ill-typed value (for example a non-logical passed to "draw") fails immediately rather than at plotting time.

    Slots

    tracktype

    "character" track type, could be peak, line, histogram, or annotation. Default is "peak". "annotation" is used to mark the peak regions. For interaction data, it could be "heatmap" or "link".

    color

    "character" track color. If the track has dat and dat2 slot, it should have two values.

    NAcolor

    "character" NA color for interactionData.

    breaks

    "numeric" breaks for color keys of interactionData.

    height

    "numeric" track height. It should be a value between 0 and 1

    marginTop

    "numeric" track top margin

    marginBottom

    "numeric" track bottom margin

    xscale

    object of xscale, describe the details of x-scale

    yaxis

    object of yaxisStyle, describe the details of y-axis

    ylim

    "numeric" y-axis range

    ylabpos

    "character", ylable postion, ylabpos should be 'left', 'right', 'topleft', 'bottomleft', 'topright', 'bottomright', 'abovebaseline', 'underbaseline', or 'none'. For gene type track, it also could be 'upstream' or 'downstream'

    ylablas

    "numeric" y lable direction. It should be a integer 0-3. See par:las

    ylabgp

    A "list" object, It will convert to an object of class gpar. This is basically a list of graphical parameter settings of y-label.

    ysplit

    A "numeric" to split y plot region for interaction data. Default is 0.5, which will split the region half to half. It will only work for back to back plot.

    dat

    Object of class GRanges, the primary data of the track. The metadata columns it must carry depend on type (see ‘Details’): coverage-like tracks ("data", "scSeq"), "lollipopData" and "interactionData" require a score column, whereas "gene" and "transcript" tracks require a feature column.

    dat2

    Object of class GRanges, the optional second data set of the track; leave it as a zero-length GRanges when unused. Its meaning depends on type:

    • for "data", "scSeq" and "lollipopData" tracks it is drawn back-to-back with dat: dat above the baseline and dat2 below it as -1 * score, which is the usual way to compare two samples or the two strands of one sample in a single panel;

    • for "interactionData" it holds the second anchor of each interaction, so it must either be the same length as dat (anchors matched element-wise) or carry a target metadata column.

    When supplied it must contain a score column, and for lollipop data every range must have width 1, exactly as for dat.

    type

    The type of track, one of:

    "data"

    continuous or interval scores — coverage, signal, peaks. Drawn as a peak, line or histogram depending on style@tracktype.

    "gene"

    gene models. dat must have a feature column describing each range (for example "exon", "CDS", "utr5", "utr3").

    "transcript"

    transcript models; same feature requirement as "gene", but isoforms are drawn on separate rows.

    "scSeq"

    single-cell signal. Validated like "data", i.e. a format and a numeric score are required.

    "lollipopData"

    point features such as variants or modification sites. Every range in dat (and dat2) must have width 1; ranges wider than one base are rejected.

    "interactionData"

    chromatin interactions, for example from Hi-C or 4C. Drawn as a heatmap or as arcs according to style@tracktype.

    format

    The format the data was imported from: "BED", "bedGraph", "WIG", "BigWig" or "BAM". It is required, and must be a single string, for "data" and "scSeq" tracks; other types ignore it. For every format except "WIG" the score column must be numeric or integer. "WIG" is the exception: because a WIG file has no fixed step boundaries until it is plotted, score is stored as a CompressedCharacterList and is converted on the fly — see importScore.

    style

    Object of class trackStyle controlling color, height, margins, y-axis, x-scale and the drawing mode. Do not assign to its slots directly; use setTrackStyleParam, setTrackXscaleParam and setTrackYaxisParam, which validate the value and update the object in the calling frame.

    name

    unused yet

    Assignment in the calling frame

    Unlike most R functions, setTrackStyleParam modifies its first argument in place: it assigns the updated track back to the variable that was passed in, so setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "color", "red") is enough and fox2 <- setTrackStyleParam(...) is not needed. This works only when ts is given as a name or a subsettable expression that can be assigned to; calling it on a temporary value, for example setTrackStyleParam(importScore(f), "color", "red"), updates nothing the caller can see. Inside lapply and friends the assignment targets the loop variable, which is discarded, so use the returned object there instead — it is returned invisibly and carries the same change.

    Like setTrackStyleParam, this method assigns the updated track back to the variable passed as ts in the caller's environment, so setTrackXscaleParam(fox2, "draw", TRUE) is sufficient and the result need not be re-assigned. It is also returned invisibly for use in contexts (such as lapply) where the calling-frame assignment has no visible target.

    Like setTrackStyleParam and setTrackXscaleParam, this method assigns the updated track back to the variable passed as ts in the caller's environment, so setTrackYaxisParam(fox2, "draw", FALSE) is sufficient on its own. It is also returned invisibly for use in contexts, such as lapply, where that calling-frame assignment has no visible target.

    See also

    Please try to use importScore and importBam to generate the object.

    setTrackXscaleParam, setTrackYaxisParam, trackStyle

    xscale, pos, setTrackStyleParam, setTrackYaxisParam

    yaxisStyle, setTrackStyleParam, setTrackXscaleParam

    Examples

    extdata <- system.file("extdata", package="trackViewer",
mustWork=TRUE)
fox2 <- importScore(file.path(extdata, "fox2.bed"), format="BED")
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "color", c("red","green"))
setTrackXscaleParam(fox2, "gp", list(cex=.5))
setTrackYaxisParam(fox2, "gp", list(col="blue"))
fox2$dat <- GRanges(score=numeric(0))

## inspect and change the style
fox2$type
#> [1] "data"
fox2$style$tracktype
#> [1] "peak"
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "tracktype", "histogram")
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "height", .2)

extdata <- system.file("extdata", package="trackViewer", mustWork=TRUE)
fox2 <- importScore(file.path(extdata, "fox2.bed"), format="BED")

## the track is updated in place; no re-assignment needed
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "tracktype", "histogram")
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "color", c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9"))
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "ylim", c(0, 50))
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "ylabpos", "topleft")
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "ylabgp", list(cex=.8, col="gray30"))
fox2$style$tracktype
#> [1] "histogram"

## inside lapply, use the returned value
trs <- lapply(list(a=fox2, b=fox2), function(.ele){
    setTrackStyleParam(.ele, "height", .25)
})

## invalid values are rejected straight away
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "ylablas", 5)      # must be 0:3
setTrackStyleParam(fox2, "xscale", list())  # use setTrackXscaleParam
} # }
extdata <- system.file("extdata", package="trackViewer", mustWork=TRUE)
fox2 <- importScore(file.path(extdata, "fox2.bed"), format="BED")

## simplest way: give a centre point and a width in bases
setTrackXscaleParam(fox2, "position",
                     list(x=122929675, y=4, label=500))
setTrackXscaleParam(fox2, "draw", TRUE)

## style the bar itself
setTrackXscaleParam(fox2, "gp", list(cex=.5, col="gray30"))

## equivalent, done by hand with explicit pos objects
setTrackXscaleParam(fox2, "from",
                     new("pos", x=122929675-500, y=4, unit="native"))
#> Found more than one class "pos" in cache; using the first, from namespace 'trackViewer'
#> Also defined by ‘motifStack’
setTrackXscaleParam(fox2, "to",
                     new("pos", x=122929675+500, y=4, unit="native"))
#> Found more than one class "pos" in cache; using the first, from namespace 'trackViewer'
#> Also defined by ‘motifStack’
setTrackXscaleParam(fox2, "label", "1K")

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## rejected: label can't be parsed as a number
setTrackXscaleParam(fox2, "position",
                     list(x=122929675, y=4, label="five hundred"))
} # }
extdata <- system.file("extdata", package="trackViewer", mustWork=TRUE)
fox2 <- importScore(file.path(extdata, "fox2.bed"), format="BED")

## show tick values at chosen positions
setTrackYaxisParam(fox2, "at", c(0, 25, 50))
setTrackYaxisParam(fox2, "label", TRUE)

## style the axis and move it to the right-hand side
setTrackYaxisParam(fox2, "gp", list(cex=.6, col="blue"))
setTrackYaxisParam(fox2, "main", FALSE)

## hide the axis entirely
setTrackYaxisParam(fox2, "draw", FALSE)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## rejected: "color" belongs to trackStyle, not yaxisStyle
setTrackYaxisParam(fox2, "color", "red")
} # }
